desc:
A minibus drives along a straight road in one direction and never turns back. It holds at most capacity passengers at any moment. Each trip is a triple [passengers, from, to]: a group of that many people gets on at position from and gets off at position to.

When a group leaves at position x and another group boards at the same position x, the leaving group is already gone before the new one boards. Return true if the bus can serve every trip without ever exceeding its capacity, otherwise false.

trips = [[2, 1, 5], [3, 3, 7]], capacity = 4  -> false  (positions 3 to 5 carry 5 people)
trips = [[2, 1, 5], [3, 5, 7]], capacity = 3  -> true
hints: The load on the bus only changes at the positions where somebody boards or leaves, so checking just those positions is enough.
Turn every trip into two events: +passengers at from and -passengers at to. Order the events by position.

At equal positions process the drop-offs before the boardings (sorting (position, delta) pairs does exactly this). Keep a running load and fail the moment it exceeds the capacity. Alternatively, use a difference array over positions 0..100,000.
editorial: Model the bus load as a function of position. A trip raises the load by passengers on the half-open stretch [from, to), so the load is the sum of all active trips. The question becomes whether the maximum of that function exceeds the capacity.

Create the events (from, +passengers) and (to, -passengers), sort them (negative deltas sort before positive ones at the same position, which implements the rule that leaving passengers are off before new ones board), and sweep while keeping a running total. If the total ever exceeds capacity, the answer is false.

Since positions are bounded by 100,000, a difference array over the positions gives the same result without sorting: add at from, subtract at to, then prefix-sum and compare each value with the capacity. Sorting costs O(m log m); the array approach costs O(m + P) where P is the largest position.
